scenes.title: A loaded map follows the selected or fixed channel

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97 on steps 1 to 4. Channel 2 does not play yet; in the next step you set it up on MIDI port 2, channel 2 with the same pattern. A saved MIDI map is loaded with two relative controls that both accumulate: CC 20 edits the velocity mask of the selected channel and CC 21 edits the velocity mask of channel 2. Both velocity masks are Off (X) and the norns shows channel 1's Device page.

steps.title: Hear both channels before any CC
steps.caption: Set up channel 2: select it (2,1), open its Device page and set its output to port 2, MIDI channel 2 with E2 and E3, press K3, give it pattern 1 with (1,2) and hold step 1 then tap step 4 to loop four steps. Select channel 1 (1,1), tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 (port 1) and channel 2 (port 2) both play velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97: no control has been moved yet.

steps.title: CC 20 on the selected channel 1
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Masks for channel 1 and select the Velocity cell, which reads X. Channel 1 is selected. Send CC 20 with value 65 eleven times (the strip shows eleven control changes). For a relative (binary offset) control, 65 means one step up, 63 means one step down and 0 also counts as down. The velocity mask starts at X, so the first step reaches 0 and the eleventh reaches 10: the Velocity cell now reads 10.

steps.title: Hear channel 1 at velocity 10
steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 1 now plays every note at velocity 10. Channel 2 is unchanged.

steps.title: CC 20 down twice
steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 twice and tap Play: channel 1 comes down from 10 to 8 and plays every note at velocity 8. Channel 2 is still unchanged.

steps.title: Select channel 2, CC 20 follows
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Masks screen stays open and its Velocity cell reads X for channel 2. Send CC 20 with value 65 three times: the cell reads 2. A selected-channel control follows the channel you select.

steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 2
steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 2 now plays at velocity 2 and channel 1 stays at 8.

steps.title: CC 21 ignores the selection
steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) to select it. Its Velocity cell still reads 8. Send CC 21 with value 65 twice, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look: its Velocity cell reads 4, up from 2. CC 21 is mapped to channel 2 itself, so it ignores which channel is selected.

steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 4
steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) again and tap Play. Channel 2 plays at velocity 4 and channel 1 stays at 8.

steps.title: CC 21 value 0 steps down
steps.caption: Send CC 21 with value 0, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look. Any value below 64 is a decrease, so its Velocity cell drops from 4 to 3.

steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 3
steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) again and tap Play. Channel 2 plays at velocity 3 and channel 1 stays at 8.

scenes.title: Announce song patterns to an Elektron receiver

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and every Mosaic option is at its default. The sequencer is stopped. The Digitakt device configuration is installed next to the test device and Elektron program changes is Off. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Choose the Digitakt device
steps.caption: On channel 1's Device screen turn E3 to the Digitakt configuration and press K3. The picker shows Digitakt: this device accepts program changes.

steps.title: Build a two-slot song
steps.caption: In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) set Global length to 4 steps, copy slot 1 into slot 2 (hold slot 1, press slot 2) and, with slot 2 selected, raise the channel octave by one (11,8) so slot 2 sounds an octave above slot 1. Return to the Song editor and select slot 1 (1,1): slot 1 is bright and slot 2 is lit.

steps.title: Play with the option Off: nothing is sent
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let it run about a second, tap Play to stop, and tap slot 2 and slot 1. With Elektron program changes at its default Off, the strip below shows notes but no program change at any point.

steps.title: Enable the option in PARAMS
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron program changes and turn E3 right to On. The row shows On. From now on Mosaic sends a program change whenever it selects or moves to a song slot; set your receiver to accept program changes.

steps.title: Select slots while stopped
steps.caption: Close the menu (K2, then K1). While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1), then slot 1 at (1,1). The strip below lists two program changes, C9 01 and then C9 00 (program values 1 and 0 on MIDI channel 10). The wire values count from 0, so the receiver selects the patterns it labels 2 and 1: receiver pattern number = Mosaic slot number.

steps.title: Hear the slot announced early
steps.caption: With slot 1 selected, tap Play (1,8), let the two four-step slots alternate for about three seconds, then tap Play again. Play first sends the program change for the slot about to sound. After that each slot change is announced once, at least half a step (about 83 ms at 90 BPM) before the new slot's first note, so the receiver has time to queue its pattern: compare the program-change times with the note times in the strip.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 and the sequencer is stopped. Channel 1's Device is the Digitakt configuration and Elektron program changes is On. Song slots 1 and 2 are four steps long and slot 2 plays an octave higher. Program changes are sent on the default channel 10.

steps.title: Set the program-change channel to 1
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron p.change channel and turn E3 left nine detents from the default 10 to 1. The row shows 1.

steps.title: The next selection uses channel 1
steps.caption: Close the menu (K2, then K1). While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1). Mosaic sends program change C0 01 (the strip shows it): program value 1 on MIDI channel 1 instead of channel 10. Set this channel to the one your receiver listens on for program changes; the default 10 suits an Elektron device left at its default.
